title: Staff Application Security Engineer
description:
Apollo .io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo .io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo .io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

Role Overview
The Staff Application Security Engineer leads application security strategy for Apollo ’s Security department and delivers it through hands-on work and technical leadership. This role takes on the hardest AppSec problems across product, platform, and AI-powered features, including problems with no established playbook.
The role shapes the roadmaps of Engineering, Product, and Platform teams so secure patterns become the default, and sets the AppSec standard that helps many teams build securely without relying on any single person.
Key Responsibilities
AppSec strategy, standards, and influence

• Lead Apollo ’s multi-year AppSec strategy and turn it into multi-quarter, cross-team initiatives that move Security department KRs. Report progress, risks, and tradeoffs to Security leadership on a regular cadence.

• Shape Engineering, Product, Platform, and Data roadmaps so security work is planned in early, and represent AppSec in cross-department decisions.

• Set the secure design, code review, and risk model standards used across the department and adjacent engineering teams, including expectations for AI-generated and agent-generated code.

• Mentor senior engineers and security champions, grow the champions program, and help raise the hiring bar, so the AppSec program does not depend on one person’s expertise.

Secure architecture and vulnerability depth

• Lead security architecture reviews and threat modeling for ambiguous, high-scale, multi-team systems, including AI and agent features, and define the approach where no precedent exists.

• Design and drive adoption of secure-by-default building blocks, such as shared authorization, safe OAuth and token handling, and SSRF-safe HTTP clients, so whole classes of issues stop appearing.

• Shape vulnerability management across internal reviews, bug bounty, pentests, and SCA and runtime findings, with a focus on root causes, bug classes, and clear risk-based severity decisions.

• Stay hands-on for the hardest cases: read code across teams, develop exploits, test bypasses, and lead variant analysis and staged remediation across teams.

Tooling, automation, and AI (AI-native by default)

• Set the standard for AI-augmented AppSec in the department. Use AI and agents for code review, threat modeling, triage, and remediation, and build automation that teams outside Security adopt, with measured gains in speed, coverage, and signal quality.

• Define how Apollo secures its AI systems and agent features, including input and output handling, AI-exposed APIs, prompt and response guardrails, tool permissions, and data-exfiltration paths.

What Good Looks Like (drafted from your mission and success sections)

• Owns AppSec strategy across a multi-year horizon and gets it committed in other teams’ roadmaps.

• Solves ambiguous, no-playbook problems and defines the approach for others to follow.

• Makes hard risk calls under ambiguity and aligns technical and non-technical leaders without formal authority.

• Builds guardrails

title: Platform Engineer

● System Architecture and Design: Design, build, and maintain the core infrastructure that runs our platforms. Develop scalable, secure and highly reliable systems to support our services.

● Performance and Reliability: Proactively monitor system performance, identify bottlenecks, and implement solutions to ensure high availability and low latency. Fill in the gaps in monitoring systems when observed.
● Incident Management: Participate in an on-call rotation to respond to production incidents. Lead incident response, conduct root cause analysis (RCA), and implement preventative measures to avoid future occurrences.
● Capacity Planning: Analyse system usage, cost and performance data to make informed decisions about resource allocation. Forecast future infrastructure needs and scale our systems accordingly.
● Collaboration and Best Practices: Work closely with software development teams to promote reliability best practices. Champion a culture of reliability across the engineering organisation.
● Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Maintain comprehensive, up-to-date documentation for all systems, processes, and operational procedures as a core part of everyday work. Treat documentation as a first-class engineering deliverable.

Accessibility and inclusivity

At Augur, our culture is built on radical candor and mutual trust. To solve the complex, physical-world problems our customers face, we need a team that thinks differently.

• Help develop solutions that balance information security needs with the needs of the business, in collaboration with team members and business and IT stakeholders.

title: GTM Engineer
description: About Kernel Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this? Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier. Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust. Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them. We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 12x YoY . The Role We're looking for a GTM Engineer to build the systems that take Kernel to $100m+ ARR. You'll own the infrastructure behind how we find, sell to and grow customers, from Salesforce and outbound to forecasting, renewals and expansion.

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

The Experimentation team's mission is to provide an insightful, reliable and easy to use experimentation platform (A/B testing and feature rollout) for customers across the company. Thousands of experiments run on our platform each year. Our team is multidisciplinary, owning a vertical stack that includes UIs for setting up and analyzing experiments, data pipelines and libraries for calculating results, and the clients and services that deliver feature flags, product configuration and experiment assignment to applications. You will work closely with data science partners, engineers across infrastructure teams, and the product engineers who use our tools every day.

Motional isn’t just building first-of-its-kind technology; we are transforming transportation to create safer streets and more sustainable mobility options.

title: Senior Backend Engineer (all genders)
description:
ABOUT BABBEL LABS

Babbel Labs is building the future of language learning. We are an AI-first, independent company within the Babbel group, based in Berlin. Our teams bring AI, research and product together to ship experiences that set a new standard for how people learn.

THE ROLE

Babbel Labs is rebuilding how learning content is created, stored and served, and how we decide what a learner sees next. The architecture for that is being set now, by a small number of engineers, and this role is one of them.

You will build and run the services behind it, in a serverless-first TypeScript and Node stack on AWS, owning them from the contract at their edge to their behaviour under load.

This is a senior individual-contributor role. You will design, build, ship and operate, and the seniority shows in the decisions you own rather than in a team reporting to you.

HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT

- Build and evolve services across our learning platform, owning each one from its API contract through to what runs in production.

- Take on services you did not write, alongside the people who did.

- Design API and data contracts that hold up over time, with type-safe transforms between the API, the domain and persistence.

- Run what you build. Instrument it, know how it fails, change live data safely, and be the person who works out why it broke.

- Deliver with coding agents as a matter of course, and verify what they produce before you rely on it.

YOUR SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

- Strong, hands-on backend engineering in TypeScript and Node as your primary working language today. We mean back-end services: not build tooling, and not the server a front-end framework happens to ship with.

- Deep, practical AWS experience in a serverless-first setting. Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB and event streaming are our daily tools, and we want someone who has designed against them rather than only deployed onto them.

- The ability to design API and data contracts and to model a domain, including type-safe transforms at the boundaries between the API, the domain and persistence.

- Real production ownership. You have instrumented your own services, understood their failure modes, changed live data without losing any, and worked incidents on systems you owned.

- Coding agents are part of your daily workflow, and you check their output before you rely on it. You are neither dismissive of them nor careless with them.

- Self-sufficiency. You get yourself unstuck in an unfamiliar codebase without a minder, and you work within its grain rather than rewriting what you have not yet understood.

- Working familiarity with infrastructure as code (Terraform) and CI/CD pipelines, enough to ship and change your own service's delivery. This is not an infrastructure role, so depth here is not the bar.

- Python as a welcome secondary language. Some of our services are Python, and a Labs engineer can expect to touch them.

NICE TO HAVE

- Go or Rust for performance-critical components. Fully optional.

- Experience with a monorepo build system and shared tooling.

- Public technical work, such as open-source contributions or writing.

WAYS OF WORKING

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role on a small team that moves fast, agent-first, but with a structured and disciplined delivery approach. It is remote and Berlin-friendly. The interview process is deliberately short: an initial screen, followed by one working session with the hiring manager.

Diversity at Babbel

As part of our ongoing journey towards building a diverse, equitable and inclusive company, we welcome everyone to apply, especially those individuals who are underrepresented in tech. We are a learning company, inside and out, and we encourage you to apply even if you do not fit all the technical requirements - all candidates are assessed based on skills, qualifications and on our business needs. title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like

•
Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.

•
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.

•
Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.

•
Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.

•
Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.

•
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.

Mines Saint-Etienne est une Ecole de l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT), 1er groupe public d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management en France. L’IMT est un EPSCP (grand établissement) sous la tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique.
L’École Nationale Supérieure des Mines de Saint-Étienne (Mines Saint-Etienne) est chargée de missions de formation, de recherche et d’innovation, de transfert vers l’industrie et de culture scientifique, technique et industrielle.

Mines Saint-Etienne représente: 2 400 élèves-ingénieurs et chercheurs en formation, 480 personnels (150 Chercheurs et Enseignants-chercheurs), un budget consolidé de 46 M€, 3 campus dédiés à l’industrie à Saint-Etienne et Lyon (région AURA), à la microélectronique et aux objets connectés à Gardanne (Métropole Aix-Marseille Provence, région SUD) et à l’ingénierie pour la santé à Saint-Etienne ; 6 unités de recherche ; 5 centres de formation et de recherche ; un centre de culture scientifique technique et industrielle leader en France « La Rotonde » (> 50 000 visiteurs / an).

Contexte scientifique et objectifs du stage :
Les dispositifs électroniques biorésorbables constituent une approche prometteuse pour le développement de systèmes électroniques temporaires, notamment dans le domaine biomédical. Ces dispositifs sont conçus pour assurer une fonction spécifique avant de se dégrader progressivement, ce qui nécessite le développement de matériaux adaptés et de solutions de stockage de l’énergie compatibles avec cette approche.
Dans ce contexte, ce stage porte sur le développement de matériaux d’électrode pour des batteries destinées aux dispositifs électroniques biorésorbables (resorbtronics). L’objectif est de préparer et de mettre en œuvre des matériaux d’électrode, puis d’étudier leurs propriétés électrochimiques afin de mieux comprendre leur comportement et d’évaluer leur potentiel pour le stockage de l’énergie.
Le/la stagiaire participera à la préparation des matériaux, à la réalisation des expériences électrochimiques ainsi qu’à l’analyse et à l’interprétation des résultats. Ce travail contribuera à identifier les paramètres influençant les performances des électrodes et à orienter leur optimisation.

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous :

• Préparer et mettre en œuvre des matériaux d’électrode pour des systèmes de stockage électrochimique de l’énergie.

• Réaliser des mesures électrochimiques afin d’évaluer les propriétés et les performances des matériaux étudiés.

• Analyser et interpréter les résultats expérimentaux, puis contribuer à l’optimisation des protocoles de préparation et de caractérisation.

• Présenter les résultats obtenus et participer aux discussions scientifiques autour du projet.

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre les Mines de Saint-Etienne ?
Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l'excellence, avec la conviction qu'ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c'est l'opportunité de trouver :

• Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un cadre de travail accueillant et un solide réseau international (T.I.M.E., EULiST).

• Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle représentant 11 millions d'euros par an, principalement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique, La Rotonde, engagé depuis 25 ans dans la médiation scientifique et accueillant plus de 50 000 visiteurs par an.

• Frais de transports en commun pris en charge à hauteur de 75% (sous conditions),

• Foyer du personnel (activités sportives, culturelles, avantages CE sur des loisirs et temps de convivialité),

DEINE AUFGABEN

Du hilfst uns bei der Erstellung, Prüfung und Verhandlung von Verträgen - alles von Verkaufs- bis Lieferverträgen oder auch Vertriebsvereinbarungen.

- Du unterstützt uns dabei, unsere Vertragsvorlagen und -richtlinien zu verbessern und immer effizienter zu machen.

- Du bist direkt dabei, wenn wir spannende kommerzielle Deals und Business Development-Projekte auf die Beine stellen.

- Du verfügst bereits über 3+ Jahre einschlägige Erfahrung in einer renommierten Anwaltskanzlei und/oder als Inhouse-Jurist:in, idealerweise mit Schwerpunkt im allgemeinen Zivilrecht sowie in den Bereichen UWG/Marketing-Claims und Markenrecht/IP

Deshalb setzen wir auf ein hybrides Arbeitskonzept, das dir die Freiheit gibt, immer genau so zu arbeiten, wie es am besten zu deinen Aufgaben passt. Millions of companies-from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups-use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Agilent is a global leader in laboratory and clinical technologies, we are passionate about bringing great science to life. We help scientists, researchers, and clinicians address some of the world’s most important challenges across life science research, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, food, environmental testing, and related markets.

Leveraging more than 50 years of expertise, we develop advanced instruments, software, consumables, and services that enable customers to generate reliable scientific results and improve scientific, economic, and operational outcomes. Our global organization combines deep technical expertise with a commitment to quality, innovation, and customer impact. We work collaboratively with our customers on their journey to make a real difference in human lives. Our culture is founded on trust, respect, and uncompromising integrity, and we pride ourselves on being a dynamic and inclusive workplace that empowers employees and fosters innovation.

The Role

Agilent is seeking a highly experienced product strategy leader to help define how laboratories will evolve over the next five to ten years and translate that vision into actionable strategies for our businesses and product organizations.
This senior individual contributor works across the enterprise at the intersection of customer insight, science, technology, and business strategy. As a recognized internal expert, you will lead high-impact, long-range initiatives, advise senior leadership, and independently solve complex challenges spanning multiple functions with limited support. You will connect external signals and customer needs with business-group priorities, product roadmaps, and execution.

• Engage scientists, laboratory leaders, executives, key opinion leaders, and strategic customers to understand current operations and emerging needs. Identify workflow bottlenecks, fragmented data, automation gaps, usability challenges, and inefficiencies that span individual instruments or product categories.

• Partner with individual business and product groups to translate enterprise insight into specific decisions about what to develop, accelerate, integrate, redesign, partner around, or stop pursuing. Convert recommendations into product concepts, roadmap changes, customer experiments, and investment cases.

• Lead initiatives across product management, R&D, commercial, digital, service, and business leadership. Align teams around customer problems that cross organizational boundaries and opportunities to combine instruments, software, consumables, automation, services, and data into more complete solutions.

title: Strategic Partnerships Director
description:
Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits.
More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan. Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings.
We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors. This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock, TPG (The Rise Fund), SoftBank, Glynn Capital, NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more.
About the role
The Director, Strategic Partnerships owns a vital piece of Human Interest 's most important growth channel: expanding our ecosystem of partners who put our retirement platform in front of millions of small and medium-sized businesses. Reporting directly to the Head of Strategic Partnerships, you will source and land business partnerships across payroll providers, benefits brokers, accountants, financial institutions, PEOs, and embedded fintech distribution.
This is an individual-contributor role with a builder's mindset and a quota orientation. You will be responsible for signing complex, multi-year agreements with some of Human Interest ’s largest and most important partners.
The role is equal parts strategist, dealmaker, and operator. You'll be just as comfortable modeling the economics of a new channel as you are in a room negotiating terms, and just as effective driving a deal across the finish line as you are shaping the partnership thesis with the CRO and the broader leadership team.
The person who thrives here is a natural hunter - energized by the pursuit of net-new relationships, comfortable opening doors cold, and relentless about carrying complex, multi-stakeholder deals through long sales cycles. You bring executive presence and the systems thinking to see how a single partnership fits into a broader distribution strategy. You read a term sheet and a partnership thesis with equal fluency, you make sharp prioritization calls about where to spend your time, and you carry deals with a sense of ownership. Above all, you are a builder: you're drawn to the ambiguity of standing up new channels from scratch, and you bring structure, pace, and judgment to a function that is still writing its own playbook.
About the team
The Partnerships organization is the engine behind Human Interest 's reach, with over 95% of our business coming from our partner ecosystem. This team builds the relationships that let us scale access to retirement benefits far faster than we could one employer at a time. They think in systems and incentives: which partners share our mission, how we make those partners successful, and how we design programs that compound over time.
The team works shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Operations to establish and launch partnerships that are commercially sound, operationally clean, and genuinely good for the businesses we ultimately serve. As we continue to scale, we're looking for a leader who can take this function to its next level: bigger partners, deeper integrations, and a measurable line on the revenue plan.

•

ABOUT TERAC

Terac is building the infrastructure for accessing human capability on demand. We are working toward a future where Terac deeply understands:

1. What every person is capable of, what they want, and where they can thrive

2. What work our customers need completed and what success requires

3. What creates a great match between the two

With this understanding, Terac can intelligently allocate human capability to the work where it creates the most value for both our experts and customers. Today, our initial wedge is providing specialized experts for AI training, evaluation, market research, and other expert-driven research.

We place 1,000s of experts per month and pay our experts, on average, over $90/hr. We're a team of 15 based in San Francisco. We've raised $16M from SignalFire, Emergence, Audacious, and SV Angel, and we work with leading AI labs and research companies.

THE PROBLEMS WE GET TO SOLVE

Terac is a two-sided marketplace, and the most interesting problems live where the money moves.

- Pricing work we've never seen before: every project is different (a cardiologist for a 30-minute interview, 200 Amharic transcribers, a team of licensed engineers building RL environments), and we have to quote it in hours, not weeks.

- Setting the right pay for experts: rates vary by domain, country, and urgency. Pay too little and the best experts walk. Pay too much and the project stops working for the customer.

- Managing spread and take rate: the gap between what customers pay and what experts earn funds everything we build, and it looks different across market research, AI training, and data collection.

- Liquidity on both sides: the right experts available the moment a customer needs them, across thousands of niches, without burning out supply or overpromising to demand.

- Moving money globally: we pay experts across dozens of countries every month, often before customers pay us, which creates real working capital, FX, and fraud challenges.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Terac is growing fast. We pay thousands of experts across dozens of countries every month, invoice a growing roster of enterprise customers, and are scaling revenue month over month. Today, finance is spread across the founders, our Chief of Staff, and outside providers.

You will be our first finance hire and own the function end to end, partnering directly with the CEO. This role owns the economics behind all of the above: pricing, pay rates, margins, and cash. You thrive in ambiguity, have exceptional judgment, and are equally comfortable building a board-ready model and reconciling a payout batch.

YOU WILL:

- Own the numbers: monthly close, accounting, revenue recognition, and reporting, working with our outside accountants and auditors.

- Run cash and payments: AR/AP, collections, and the global contributor payout engine that pays thousands of experts every month across many countries and payment rails.

- Build planning and forecasting: budgets, burn, hiring plans, and the operating model, plus project-level margin analysis and pricing support for deals.

- Support fundraising and the board: investor updates, data rooms, and diligence for future rounds.

- Build the systems: choose and implement tooling (ERP, spend management, payroll, billing) and the controls that let us scale 10x.

- Handle compliance: sales tax, 1099s and international contractor compliance, insurance, and corporate filings with our legal partners.

YOU HAVE:

- 3-7+ years in finance or accounting, ideally a mix of Big 4, banking, or consulting and a high-growth startup

- Hands-on experience owning close, cash management, and financial modeling

- Comfort building systems from scratch and working with ambiguous, messy data

- Strong judgment and the ability to prioritize under pressure

YOU LIKELY HAVE EXPERIENCE IN:

- Finance at an early-stage or high-growth startup, often as the first or second finance hire

- Marketplaces, payments, or businesses with high-volume global

title: Marketing Agency Client Account Coordinator
description:

Working Hours: 20-30 hours per week, within agreed working blocks between 11:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time
About the Role
We are looking for a proactive and highly organized Client Account Coordinator to support client relationships and project delivery within a marketing agency. In this role, you will work closely with law-firm clients, helping ensure smooth onboarding, clear communication, and timely delivery of projects. You will lead client calls, provide regular updates, track deadlines and approvals, and follow through on deliverables. You will also use AI tools and established playbooks to support fulfillment, while carefully reviewing all AI-generated content against source material before it is shared with clients.
Key Responsibilities
Client Account Management

• Support the onboarding of new law-firm clients and ensure a smooth transition into the agency's processes.

• Lead client calls, answer questions, and provide clear updates throughout active projects.

• Maintain strong, professional relationships with clients through proactive communication.

Project Coordination

• Track project deadlines, deliverables, approvals, and outstanding action items.

• Follow up with clients and internal team members to ensure projects continue moving forward.

• Send clear and timely weekly updates through Slack.

AI & Fulfillment Support

• Use AI tools and internal playbooks to support client fulfillment and project delivery.

• Review and verify AI-generated output against original source material before it reaches clients.

• Flag any issues, inconsistencies, or major changes for approval when needed.

Communication & Follow-Through

• Keep clients and internal stakeholders informed about project progress and next steps.

• Ensure no deadlines, approvals, or deliverables fall through the cracks.

• Escalate pricing decisions, upsells, and significant changes to the appropriate team member for approval.

Required Experience & Skills

• At least 2 years of experience in client account management, agency coordination, project coordination, or a similar client-facing role.

• Professional spoken and written English, with the confidence to lead client calls and communicate clearly in writing.

• Professional Spanish communication skills.

• Strong organizational and project management abilities, with experience managing deadlines and multiple priorities.

• Experience working with clients in a marketing agency or professional services environment is highly preferred.

• Familiarity with AI tools and the ability to carefully review AI-generated content for accuracy.

• Strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to follow-ups and problem-solving.

Perfect Fit / Culture

• You take ownership of client accounts and follow through without needing constant reminders.

• You communicate confidently and professionally, whether leading a live client call or sending a written update.

• You are highly organized and make sure deadlines, approvals, and action items are always tracked.

• You understand that AI output needs human review and take responsibility for checking accuracy before work reaches a client.

• You know when to handle an issue independently and when to escalate decisions that require approval.

Typical Day
Your day may begin by reviewing active client accounts, checking upcoming deadlines, and following up on outstanding approvals. You may lead a client call to answer questions or discuss project progress, then update the team and client on next steps.
Throughout the day, you will coordinate deliverables, use internal playbooks and AI tools to support fulfillment, and carefully review work before it is shared externally. You will also send updates through Slack and make sure every client has clear visibility into the progress of their projects.

Loan Documentation Preparation: Prepare and review SBA loan closing documents for compliance with SBA guidelines and lender requirements, ensuring accuracy and completeness in every document.

Training and Mentorship: Serve as a resource and mentor for new team members, offering guidance on SBA requirements, documentation standards, and best practices for efficient loan processing and closing.

title: Sales Development Representative
description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We are looking for a passionate and motivated Sales Development Representative with a love for selling and a tenacious and methodical approach to prospecting.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Create a fantastic first impression with prospects and customers while building pipeline for Account Executives.

- Follow up and qualify inbound requests and MQLs, via the telephone and email, for scientific fit.

- Organize, categorize, and prioritize sales leads in Salesforce and measure lead conversion and performance against quota.

- Leverage prospecting tools to research companies and identify key decision makers at new accounts.

- Develop customized pitches for different target accounts and personas.

- Work with Account Executives to drive outbound prospecting activities, including cold calling, emailing, and communicating our value proposition to decision makers.

- Work with the field marketing and sales teams to drive attendance at Benchling field events such as executive dinners and happy hours.

- Staff tradeshows and follow-up on leads collected at the Benchling booth.

QUALIFICATIONS

- Undergraduate degree in life sciences required (e.g. molecular biology, biotechnology, biomedical engineering, biochemistry), Postgraduate welcomed

- Recent graduate or 1-2 years of internship / work experience in a Sales Development Representative, Business Development Representative function.

- Passionate about Benchling’s mission and the acceleration of life sciences research

- Not afraid to pick up the phone and cold call in German

- Strong verbal and written communication skills in German and English

- Persistent, self-motivated, and willing to go beyond strict job responsibilities

- Driven to meet/exceed goals with a proven history of consistent high achievement

- Gritty and resourceful

- Methodical and disciplined work ethic

- Language Requirements: English AND German

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

title: Financial Partnerships Operations Manager, Americas
description:
ABOUT AIRWALLEX

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles https://www.airwallex.com/en-us/operating-principles to see it in full.

 

How you'll make impact

Financial Partnerships Operations is essential to maintaining Airwallex’s relationships with financial partners as our Americas network grows. You’ll help keep live partner work moving while building the infrastructure and operating mechanisms that make the function more scalable.

- Own day-to-day operations across Airwallex’s financial partner network in the Americas, including onboarding, offboarding, account management and partner requests.

- Manage partner requirements and deliverables across Risk, Legal, Compliance, Product and Operations, using sound judgment to assess requests, identify gaps and keep things moving.

- Build scalable processes and resources to manage partner information, including repositories, playbooks, QBRs and reporting.

- Build strong relationships with financial partners and identify opportunities to improve processes and operational performance as the business grows.

This role is hybrid, based in New York, NY.

What we're looking for

Essentials

- 4+ years of experience in fintech, financial services, payments, banking or a related field.

- Experience managing complex projects and deliverables across teams such as Risk, Legal, Compliance, Product and Operations.

- Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, dependencies and escalations through to completion.

- Strong judgment and attention to detail, with the ability to assess requests, identify gaps and push back when needed.

- Strong communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with senior stakeholders and external partners.

- Analytical and organized, with the ability to track performance, identify risks and work autonomously in a changing environment.

Preferred

- Experience with banks, payment processors, card schemes or other regulated financial institutions.

- Familiarity with KYC, KYB, due diligence or financial crime compliance.

- Understanding of payment flows, acquiring, issuing, scheme rules or technical integrations.

- Experience building scalable processes, dashboards, partner scorecards or playbooks.

- Experience using AI or automation to improve processes and reduce manual work.

- Spanish-language skills.

You'll thrive here if

- You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.

- You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway.

- You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching. Quality and accountability aren't external expectations; they're internal ones.

- You enjoy working closely with people across multiple countries and time zones as part of one connected, global team, including flexing your hours occasionally to make that connection work.

- You over-communicate by design. You'd rather flag something early than let it become a surprise.

- You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.
